title: Controls never cover text or leave the screen
statement: No control or pop-up may cover reading text or leave the screen at any width, even after a resize.
example: After the window narrowed with a definition open, the pop-up sat at left 328.59 px and right 640.59 px in a 390 px viewport.
detail: At phone and tablet widths a fixed view toggle sat over the end of a passage's first sentence and hid part of a word, with no tooltip open. A glossary definition opened at laptop width stayed at left 328.59 px, right 640.59 px in a 390 px viewport after the window narrowed, and page-level overflow checks did not catch it. Beside a long answer, an undo label collapsed into a narrow column 37.27px wide, and the expected fix reserves the control's space independently of the answer's length.
against: The pop-up case holds only for a resize while it is open: "Scope: confirmed for a viewport change with the popover already open. Opening it fresh on mobile fits; reopening is a workaround." (grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/staging-full-sweep/README.md, line 47)

evidence.quote: The fixed view toggle sits over the end of the first sentence, hiding part of “sleep.”
Reading content should remain unobstructed by controls.
Its measured bounds are left **328.59 px**, right **640.59 px**, width **312 px** in a **390 px** viewport.
Expected: reposition the open definition inside the viewport or dismiss it when layout changes.
Expected: a stable readable undo label, with space reserved independently of the answer length.
